entry.title: Limits on preparing light states via phase-space majorization
entry.summary: Fundamental limits on photonic state preparation from phase-space majorization arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies probabilistic conversions between quantum states of light, deriving fundamental bounds for both exact and approximate transformations. The authors develop a theory of weak, fully relative majorization that compares the disorder of phase-space functions. Focusing on Wigner functions in multimode photonic systems, they establish no-go results and tradeoff relations for conversions involving squeezed, cat, Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill, and Fock states. The work derives novel bounds and recovers known tight ones. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a phase-space relative majorization theory yielding new no-go bounds and tradeoffs for photonic state preparation, recovering known tight bounds.

entry.title: Decorrelating AI Advice Layers to Reduce Synchronized Liquidation in Agentic Wealth Management
entry.summary: Decorrelating the Advice Layer: A Calibrated Fragility Metric and Tested Mitigations for Synchronized Liquidation in Agentic Wealth Management arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper models conversational AI agents that run continuous market analysis, allocation, and execution for wealth management clients, calibrated to model concentration, retail turnover, and 33 years of equity returns. It finds that the effective number of independent decision-makers is bounded, and that synchronized automation rather than model concentration drives market-wide tail losses. A fragility index built from aggregate flow, public returns, and impact estimates forecasts tail liquidation out of sample better than concentration or correlation measures. Dispersing overlay parameters, staging execution, and adding a participation breaker together cut tail liquidation by 63 percent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an aggregate-flow fragility index and report that synchronized automation, not model concentration, drives tail liquidation in simulations and historical replays.

entry.title: A differentiable watershed layer for trainable segmentation networks
entry.summary: The Power Watershed as a Differentiable Segmentation Layer arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper places a Power Watershed, the limit of a seeded Random Walker as its edge-weight exponent grows, at the end of a segmentation network so it can be trained end to end. The finite-exponent solve is exactly differentiable through one adjoint solve. On PanNuke nuclei segmentation, the layer turns a U-Net into an instance segmenter, raising instance F1 from 0.656 to 0.795. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed a differentiable Power Watershed layer at the end of a U-Net and report instance F1 rising from 0.656 to 0.795 on PanNuke nuclei segmentation.

entry.title: Predicting the Reward, Not the World: Training Models to Choose Better ML Programs
entry.summary: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes World Reward Models (WRMs) for search-based machine-learning agents, which learn directly from real execution results which candidate program will perform better, instead of predicting intermediate execution outcomes. The proposed model, ForeCritic, picks the better program 79.4% of the time on 12,438 held-out pairs from 26 ML tasks, compared with 53% to 62% for general-purpose LLM judges. When integrated into AIDE, ML-Master, and ForeAgent, it cuts mean task time by 4.4 to 7.5 times while keeping mean scores within 0.01 or raising them. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose world reward models that directly select the better candidate program without predicting execution outcomes, report proofs and 12,438 held-out pair evaluations, and test speedups w

entry.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
entry.summary: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies self-improving LLM agents that edit their own prompts and rules, keeping edits only when an acceptance gate scores them higher on task batches. Because overlapping safeguards mask the effect of deleting one, the gate can approve harmful changes based on task success alone, eroding redundancy unseen. The authors measured harm across all subsets of four safeguards in two environments, running 411 improvement loops under ten gate rules. They also report that evaluation batch size and the statistical test used affect which safeguards are kept. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show acceptance gates erode redundant safeguards via masking, reporting 411 controlled loops and a frozen predictive model.

entry.title: Reliable, scalable, value-aligned generative recommendation for large-scale advertising (GR4AD-X)
entry.summary: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents GR4AD-X, an advertising recommendation framework for the Kuaishou platform that generates discrete semantic identifiers autoregressively. It improves semantic identifier reliability with Multi-Path assignment, scales model capacity along several dimensions under serving constraints, and aligns generation with commercial value through the UniVGD method. Large-scale online A/B tests on Kuaishou's advertising platform show a 3.07% cumulative revenue gain over the deployed GR4AD baseline while meeting latency and throughput requirements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose Multi-Path SID assignment, multi-dimensional capacity scaling, and unified value alignment, reporting a 3.07% revenue gain in large-scale Kuaishou online A/B tests.

entry.title: Optimal Regret Bounds for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning
entry.summary: Optimal Regret for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies decentralized online convex optimization where networked learners minimize a sequence of global losses using only local losses and compressed messages from neighbors. The authors propose Ascent-gossip, which combines an online compression strategy with a Chebyshev recursion to reach consensus faster than existing compressed gossip methods. Using this method, they present an online algorithm whose regret bounds for convex and strongly convex losses match known lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine online compression with Chebyshev recursion, reporting regret bounds matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics
entry.summary: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Bisimulation metrics measure task-relevant state similarity in reinforcement learning, but existing constructions mostly cover discounted MDPs. This paper reinterprets these metrics as game value functions of zero-sum turn-based games, giving unique definitions for total- and average-reward settings. It also analyzes how metric finiteness depends on MDP structure and shows that the metrics bound total-reward and optimal relative value differences. Error and suboptimality guarantees for aggregation-based planning are provided. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast bisimulation metrics as zero-sum game values, giving unique definitions for undiscounted total- and average-reward MDPs, with bounds on value differences and aggregation-planning er

entry.title: ParaTTT: Parallelizing Test-Time Training Layers with Deep Memories
entry.summary: ParaTTT: Parallelizing Test-Time Training Layers with Deep Memories arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces ParaTTT (PTTT), an algorithm that parallelizes deep nonlinear memories in test-time training layers by iteratively refining estimates of the inner-loop gradient trajectory. Each refinement uses three chunkwise-parallel passes, and the exact online gradient descent recurrence is a fixed point of the iteration. With two refinement steps at 4K context, the inner-loop evaluation is reported to be 32 times faster than TTT-MLP with block approximation at matched error, and the 340M model trains 4.9 times faster. Models at 340M and 1.3B parameters match or exceed Gated DeltaNet and Mamba-2 on language-modeling perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, with better recall than linear recurrences. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose iterative chunkwise-parallel refinement for deep nonlinear test-time training memories, report 340M and 1.3B model comparisons, and give a convergence proof for a two-layer variant

entry.title: Near-optimal regret for adversarial linear bandits under strong corruption
entry.summary: Nearly Minimax Optimal Regret for Adversarial Linear Bandits with Strong Corruptions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies adversarial linear bandits where a strong adversary corrupts observed rewards after seeing the learner's action, within a known total corruption budget C. The authors propose CRW-FTRL, which uses a radius-weighted entropy regularizer and a normalized kernel estimator whose corruption sensitivity depends on per-action radii. The algorithm achieves regret that matches the best corruption-free rate and the corruption lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Applied to discretized general compact action sets, it yields regret of order d√T plus dC. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a radius-weighted regularizer achieving near-minimax regret under strong corruption, matching the corruption-free rate up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent AI
entry.summary: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines demographic bias when clinical large language models operate as multi-agent teams. Testing five model families and four aggregation topologies on 120 MIMIC-IV emergency cases with counterfactual demographic swaps, all configurations preserved the direction of individual agents' answers, giving Black patients more acute triage. The authors report that fairness instructions and demographic masking did not close the gap, while a diverse-perspective ensemble that pools counterfactual versions during deliberation reduced the disparity by 67 to 94%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce disparity laundering and report a full factorial of five model families and four topologies on 120 MIMIC-IV cases under counterfactual swaps.

entry.title: Is It My Preference? A Role Grounding Attack That Misattributes Preferences in Agent Memory
entry.summary: Is it my preference? Role Grounding Attack against Agent's Memory via Social Interaction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026LLM-based agents share experiences on social platforms and remember new preferences, but existing memory systems can misattribute roles to principals. The paper formalizes the Role Grounding Attack (RGA), which uses nested conversations so that a victim agent records an attacker's preference as the victim user's preference. The authors instantiate RGA as tool selection manipulation and privacy leakage, and evaluate it across five memory systems and six language models. Both attack types achieve high success rates, which the authors argue calls for stronger role grounding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize Role Grounding Attack, exploiting role misattribution in agent memory, and report evaluations across five memory systems and six models for tool manipulation and privacy leakage.

entry.title: Annealed, Averaged Markov Chains Reach the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA (Part II: Langevin Dynamics)
entry.summary: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part II: Langevin Dynamics arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies tensor principal components analysis on the sphere, where an unknown vector must be recovered from a noisy observation of its k-th tensor power. The authors show that spherical Langevin dynamics, combined with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization. Together with Part I, the results show that local Markov chains can succeed down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show annealed, averaged spherical Langevin dynamics recovers tensor PCA signal in polynomial time above the algorithmic threshold from random initialization, continuing Part I.

entry.title: Toffoli gates with no spare qubits, and T-gate counts for Boolean oracles
entry.summary: Ancilla-free randomized Toffoli gates and the T-count of Boolean oracles arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the T-gate cost of Boolean oracles in fault-tolerant Clifford+T circuits. The authors compute sampled parities in place on the gate's own controls, which removes the need for extra qubits once the gate is large enough, using about 8 T gates per bit of precision per random circuit. The same holds for exclusive-ors of affine subspace indicators. The paper also shows that a random set of fixed density needs exponentially many T gates at constant error, whereas an affine subspace of the same density needs a constant number. ★★★★ Notable: The authors remove extra ancilla qubits from the Gosset et al. randomized Toffoli construction, using about 8 T gates per bit of precision, and compare against lower bounds.

entry.title: DecompGym: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Designing Decomposition Algorithms
entry.summary: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces DecompGym, a benchmark of 81 optimization instances from nine problem families, including five Benders and four column generation tasks, where agents must write solvers for prescribed decomposition methods. Each solver is checked for running within 60 seconds, numerical feasibility, an LLM judge's audit of the method used, and an objective within 1% of the stored optimum. Evaluating 12 GPT, Claude, and Gemini models over up to ten attempts, the authors find that reflection, which diagnoses failures first, succeeds on 66% of retries versus 39% for independent regeneration. The study concludes that decomposition agents need checks on how a solver reaches its answer, not only output checks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a 81-instance benchmark testing LLM agents on Benders and column generation, comparing regeneration with reflection across 12 models, and separating output checks from method audits.

entry.title: Theoretical Limits and Guarantees for Graph-Based Nearest-Neighbor Search
entry.summary: On Worst-Case Guarantees for Graph-Based Nearest-Neighbor Search arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies the theoretical guarantees of graph-based nearest neighbor search methods such as HNSW, DiskANN, and NSG, which perform well in practice. The authors prove that standard graph-based methods running greedy search on flat or hierarchical graphs cannot achieve sublinear query time in Euclidean space, even with arbitrarily large approximation factors. They show that allowing Steiner points in the search graph makes sublinear query time possible, with bounds comparable to LSH, and include initial experiments on incorporating Steiner points into practical methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove standard graph-based search cannot achieve sublinear query time, and that Steiner points yield LSH-comparable bounds, with initial experiments.

entry.title: What LOL Measures: Hidden Label Shifts in Low-Light Enhancement Benchmarks
entry.summary: What Does LOL Measure? Hidden Label Shifts in Low-Light Enhancement Benchmarks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper audits the standard low-light image enhancement benchmarks LOL-v1 and LOLv2-Real using 18 public checkpoints from eight methods. It finds that test labels differ from training labels, with LOL-v1 test labels rendered differently and LOLv2-Real test labels darker than its training labels. The authors show that test-set checkpoint selection and released test-time settings affect reported scores and method rankings, and they provide reporting recommendations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors audit 18 checkpoints of eight methods, report hidden label shifts in LOL benchmarks, and quantify their effect on rankings.

entry.title: Post-training LLMs with LLMON for safer instruction handling
entry.summary: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a post-training method using LLMON (LLM Object Notation), which separates executable instructions from passive data and requires identifier-based execution. The authors built a 4.6B-token structured training corpus and post-trained Granite-4.1 3B and 8B base models with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. They report that attack success rates on indirect prompt-injection benchmarks fell from 53-100% to 0.02-5.6% while general capabilities were preserved. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that LLMON-structured post-training cuts indirect prompt-injection success rates substantially on two Granite models, and introduce attention-based interpretability metrics.

entry.title: SPARSEBLEED: A Hardware Attack Bypassing Privacy Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations
entry.summary: SPARSEBLEED: Bypassing Attribute-Inference Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents SparseBleed, a hardware-level attack that infers sensitive input attributes from a single query by exploiting timing signatures of sparsity-driven execution paths in accelerators. It works across Intel AVX2/AVX-512/AMX, NVIDIA Ampere Tensor Cores, and several sparse and dense libraries. The authors evaluate the attack on Texas-100X and compare mitigations, finding that disabling sparsity optimizations is costly while a padding defense adds about 7.24% average overhead. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a hardware-level attribute-stealing attack exploiting sparsity timing, reporting 66.39% Sex inference on Texas-100X and evaluating a padding defense's overhead.

entry.title: Predicting Which Pages AI Answer Engines Cite, with Open Models and a 4B Student
entry.summary: Predicting What Answer Engines Cite: Open Decision Models, Rerankers and a Distilled 4B Student on Ten Engines under Controlled Retrieval arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to rank candidate web pages by how often answer engines will cite them in generated responses. The authors evaluate pretrained rerankers, a hosted decision model, eight open decision models, and distilled students on GEO-Bench queries across ten engines. A 4B student model fine-tuned from Qwen3-Reranker-4B performs comparably to the strongest scorers, and the model, benchmark, predictions, and code are released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report comparing rerankers and distilled 4B students against teacher decision models on GEO-Bench across ten answer engines.

entry.title: Vision Tomography: Portable 3D Face-Skull Reconstruction from Visual Data
entry.summary: Vision Tomography: Towards Portable 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Inference from Visual Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Vision Tomography (VT), a framework that reconstructs paired 3D face and skull geometry from visual inputs such as images or sketches. The authors built a dataset of over 200 cases with CT skulls, CT faces, and textured face scans, and proposed a 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Morphable Model (BFSM) that infers shape between face and skull via a shared coefficient space. The framework is demonstrated in forensic and medical applications, including paired reconstruction and predicting surgical outcomes through joint face-skull editing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a bidirectional face-skull morphable model and a 200-plus sample dataset for paired 3D reconstruction from visual data, reporting experiments in forensic and medical applications.

entry.title: How Open-Source Software Adopts Post-Quantum Cryptography: Practices and Challenges
entry.summary: Understanding Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption: Practices, Challenges, and Evolution in Open-Source Software arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper mines 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 open-source repositories to study how projects implement and maintain post-quantum cryptography (PQC) support. About 90% of PQC-related commits concern maintenance of existing support, and build, packaging, dependency, and functional failures account for roughly half of the categorized issues. After the 2024 NIST standards were finalized, standardized algorithm names appeared in more than 80% of analyzed PQC changes, but first implementations did not significantly increase. ★★★★ Notable: The authors mine 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 repositories, building an 11-category taxonomy of PQC challenges and releasing the dataset and pipeline.

entry.title: Random Centres and the ε-Dependence of Constant-Round Planar Domination
entry.summary: Random Centres and the ǎrepsilon-Dependence of Constant-Round Planar Domination arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies constant-round LOCAL algorithms for minimum dominating set on planar graphs. It replaces the heaviest-edge star selection in the clustering step with a random-centre rule, which reduces the round-complexity exponent. The authors also analyse how the approximation parameter ε affects the number of rounds, showing Ω(1/ε) rounds are needed on paths and Θ(1/ε) rounds are optimal on forests and outerplanar graphs. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces heaviest-edge star selection with random centres, reducing the planar round exponent from about 25.81 to below 5.89, with lower bounds reported.

entry.title: Who Else Is In? How AI Agents Might Start Secret Collusion Using Vague Messages
entry.summary: Who Else Is In? Multi-Agent Collusion Initation Via Strategic Vagueness arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how multi-agent LLM systems could begin collusion, with agents using vague public messages to find hidden partners while appearing to do ordinary work. The authors run a mutual identification game in which two agents must recognize each other while solving a shared task, and some models succeed without explicit guidance, often evading monitors at low false positive rates. They report that as messages grow more indirect, monitor punishment can fall faster than partner coordination, creating a profitable middle ground. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a mutual identification game showing strategic vagueness can initiate collusion past monitors; the abstract reports successful handshakes and an asymmetric monitor-punishment ver

entry.title: Encore: Turning Public Exploit PoCs into Threat Hunting Rules
entry.summary: Set an Exploit to Catch an Exploit: Compiling Public Proofs of Concept into Threat Hunting Rules arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper observes that public exploit code for new vulnerabilities usually appears before detection rules for their exploitation. The authors present Encore, which compiles a public Python proof-of-concept exploit into CVE-specific hunting rules over a web service's existing logs, without running the code. The paper reports that Encore's rules find 43 of 45 evaluated CVEs, separate exploit payloads from harmless matched requests, and raise no alerts across 27,081 legitimate and crawl requests. ★★★★ Notable: The authors compile public PoC exploits into hunting rules without execution, reporting results on 45 CVEs against Splunk's public attack data.

entry.title: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions
entry.summary: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes Human-Residual Steering (HRS), a method that aligns frozen large language model judges with the distribution of individual human ratings by learning hidden-state interventions. Across 14 benchmarks and four judges from three model families, HRS outperforms all evaluated frozen-weight baselines on distribution matching. It also trains about 88 times fewer parameters than distributional fine-tuning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose learned hidden-state interventions to align frozen LLM judges with human distributions, reporting gains across 14 benchmarks with far fewer trained parameters.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
entry.summary: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies conformal prediction under covariate shift when the covariate density ratio is known, aiming for prediction sets with minimal expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, the authors prove that combining an inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes expected length among all rules valid over the weighted-exchangeability class. They approximate the oracle with quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling. Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, set length, and runtime with existing methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the inverse-density score with randomized weighted calibration minimizes expected set length over weighted-exchangeable rules, and report experiments on 36 density configurations and

entry.title: Lower bound for projection-free online learning with linear oracles
entry.summary: An Ω(T³/4) lower bound for projection-free online learning with linear minimization oracles arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies projection-free online learning algorithms that handle the decision set using linear minimization oracles. Prior work showed that Online Frank-Wolfe achieves regret scaling as T^{3/4} under specific tunings, but whether all tunings do so was open. The authors prove a universal worst-case regret lower bound of Ω(T^{3/4} m^{-1/4}) for any projection-free algorithm making at most m oracle calls per round. They also propose an extended Online Frank-Wolfe that uses multiple linear optimizations per round and prove a regret upper bound of O(max{T^{3/4} m^{-1/4}, √T}). ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a universal regret lower bound for projection-free algorithms and match it with an extended OFW upper bound, answering an open question.

entry.title: Early Signs of Feature Learning in Deep Linear Networks
entry.summary: Investigating the Early Signatures of Feature Learning in Deep Linear Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper analyzes features learned by a deep linear network in a mean-field parameterization after a single gradient step from initialization, using high-dimensional data with a low-dimensional spiked signal. It derives closed-form expressions for the bias, variance, and generalization error of kernel ridge regression on these features. A one-step generalization advantage appears only when spike strength and effective signal-to-noise ratio are sufficiently large, and it vanishes for isotropic inputs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a closed-form account of one-step feature learning in mean-field deep linear networks and derive bias, variance, and generalization error expressions.

entry.title: Measuring Where Intent Is Lost When AI Agents Write Smart Contracts
entry.summary: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether AI agents that write smart contracts from plain-English descriptions actually produce code that behaves as requested. The authors compare an AI-written contract with the original on the same transactions and find that common AI judges and standard analysis tools miss obvious mistakes. They propose asking the client clarifying questions before code generation and checking the result against an independently written executable answer key, which they report works far better than reviewing or patching afterwards. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose asking clarifying questions before generation and checking against an independent executable answer key, reporting results on 600 tasks across three models and releasing tools.

entry.title: Choosing Random Mixtures of AI Versions with Fewest Stakeholder Rejections
entry.summary: Learning Lotteries with Minimal Stakeholder Violations from Membership Queries arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies how to pick a randomized mixture of several candidate AI system versions that the fewest stakeholders reject. Each stakeholder accepts only mixtures inside an unknown halfspace, and the developer can learn this only by asking yes-or-no membership queries. The authors show that minimizing rejections is APX-hard in general, give exact algorithms for special cases, and provide approximation guarantees when only some stakeholders can be queried. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model stakeholder acceptance as unknown halfspaces, prove APX-hardness for minimizing rejections, and give polynomial and quasi-polynomial exact algorithms with sampling guarantees, plus s

entry.title: TACOS: Terrain-aware contact supervision method for visual footstep planning
entry.summary: TACOS: Terrain-Aware COntact Supervision for Visual Footstep Planning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents TACOS, a method that builds a footstep instability score from the residual of a factor graph used in legged robot state estimation, then projects that score onto earlier camera images to train a dense visual predictor. It proposes a hard score that uses hindsight and a causal soft score available immediately. On 1716 manually annotated contacts and three outdoor test runs, both variants outperform the compared alternatives at detecting instability and ranking its severity. In a real-world 50 m forest trial, the trained predictor handles mud and vegetation and steps around fallen branches. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a footstep instability score from factor-graph residuals to supervise a visual predictor, compared against baselines on 1716 annotated contacts and outdoor runs.

entry.title: WebAnything: Automatically Building Reusable Web Environments from Real Sites for AI Agents
entry.summary: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments arXiv · Oct 28, 2026WebAnything is a framework that automatically rebuilds reusable, resettable website environments from real URLs, so web agents can be trained and tested without manual per-site setup. It constructed 244 website environments across 14 application domains, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. In a blind audit it outperformed the human-assisted WebHarbor on three fidelity metrics. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improved success rates on several benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors automate reconstruction of reusable web environments from real URLs with an independent verifier, reporting 244 sites and gains from fine-tuning on 5,856 trajectories.

entry.title: Backdoors in AI agents planted through poisoned pretraining data
entry.summary: Agentic Backdoors via Pretraining Poisoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The authors pretrained Qwen3 models from scratch at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B sizes, then post-trained each into a command-line agent. They show that poisoning just 0.1% of the pretraining corpus can implant a backdoor that makes the agent execute attacker-chosen commands on a user's machine when a trigger is present, while behaving normally otherwise. Attack success rate rises with model size, reaching about 92% for the 4B model at a 0.1% poison rate, and remains positive even at 0.0005%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show pretraining poisoning can implant a remote code execution backdoor in agents, reporting about 92% attack success for a 4B Qwen3 model at a 0.1% poison rate.

entry.title: When Skills Tell Agents Not to Ask: A Study of Oversight-Loosening Directives in AI Agent Skills
entry.summary: When Skills Tell Agents Not to Ask: A Large-Scale Study of Oversight Directives in Agent Skills arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies oversight-loosening directives in agent skills, reusable instruction packages built around a SKILL.md file, such as instructions to proceed without approval or to bypass checks with --no-verify. The authors analyzed 1.53 million English skills from GitSkills, hand-labeled 2,097 units, and trained a detector to scale the analysis. About one in seventeen skills contains such a directive, and skills that run shell code, install packages, or use sudo are more likely to contain one. Existing open-source scanners catch at most 46% of these directives with low precision. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first large-scale study of oversight-loosening directives, analyzing 1.53 million skills, hand-labeling 2,097 units, and training a detector to scale.

entry.title: FVH-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generator Safety Beyond Obviously Harmful Pictures
entry.summary: FVH-Bench: Evaluating Image Generator Safety Beyond Overtly Harmful Imagery arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper defines functional visual harm (FVH) as the risk from what generated images enable, such as instructions or deceptive artifacts, rather than only what they depict. The authors introduce FVH-Bench, which contains 669 prompts covering five harmful visual functions and ten risk domains. Evaluation of 11 image generators found they rarely refuse these requests and often produce artifacts that fulfill the harmful functions. Existing safety detectors also show limited coverage of FVH. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose functional visual harm and a 669-prompt benchmark, evaluating 11 image generators and existing safety detectors beyond overtly harmful content.

entry.title: How much a weight update changes a model, compared across training stages
entry.summary: What a Weight Update Buys: Leverage Across Training Stages arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces leverage, a measure of how much a unit of weight change affects a language model's behavior, and applies it to released Olmo-3, Tülu-3, Zephyr, and OLMo-2 checkpoints. It finds that pretraining updates act like random directions on prose, while SFT, RL, and DPO stages show much higher leverage, up to about 23,000 for DPO. The authors also study how training precision and DARE random drop-and-rescale affect these measurements. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce leverage, a Fisher-form measure of weight update effect, comparing training stages across released checkpoints and deriving a DARE reuse law.

entry.title: Relevance-guided residual calibration for compressing dense retrieval embeddings
entry.summary: Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration for Spectral Compression of Dense Retrieval Embeddings arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses spectral compression of dense retrieval embeddings, noting that existing corpus-derived weighting rules do not account for each retained direction's contribution to relevance. The authors propose Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration (RRC), a closed-form method that uses relevance judgments to refine spectral weights while preserving the compressor's overall trend. entry.title: Network Structure Doesn't Matter: Classical Consensus Theory Fails for LLM Groups
entry.summary: Network Topology Does Not Matter: The Breakdown of Classical Consensus in LLM Populations arXiv · Oct 25, 2026This paper studies how networks of multiple large language models reach collective agreement. entry.summary: Barriers to Identity-Based Encryption in Generic Group-Action Models IACR ePrint · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether identity-based encryption (IBE) can be built from the basic interface of generic cryptographic group actions. entry.title: An algebraic data structure for fast polynomial evaluation over large-characteristic fields
entry.summary: An Algebraic Polynomial Evaluation Datastructure for Fields of Large Characteristic IACR ePrint · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies data structures that evaluate a multivariate polynomial at any input point by using random access to a precomputed encoding of the polynomial. The authors construct algebraic curves over prime fields by using the base-β representation of prime field elements, reducing evaluation recursively to points in boxes of decreasing size. The resulting structure greatly improves the dependence of query complexity on the characteristic p and removes p from the data structure size. entry.summary: Radical isogenies on every model IACR ePrint · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies radical isogeny formulae, which compute a cyclic chain of N-isogenies using one N-th root per step without sampling torsion points. entry.summary: Falcon Key Recovery from Joint Sampler Leakages IACR ePrint · Oct 27, 2026Falcon and the FN-DSA standard based on it create signatures using discrete Gaussian sampling, and power consumption during this step leaks information about secret-dependent values. entry.title: Quantum key distribution secured by a bound on information leakage
entry.summary: Prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution from a bound on information leakage arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether, in prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution, a single bound on information leakage from the sender's source can replace a detailed model of the source. entry.summary: SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching (Extended Version) arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Data memory-dependent prefetchers (DMPs) are a CPU optimization in recent mainstream processors that can improve performance but may leak secrets through side channels. entry.summary: MiCo: Mutual Information Coverage Optimization through Semantic Erasure Modeling for Efficient MLLM Inference arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Multimodal large language models incur high computational costs when processing many visual tokens. entry.title: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Using After-the-Fact Experience to Build Advance Foresight
entry.summary: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Turning Post-hoc Experiences into Prior Foresight arXiv · Oct 6, 2026This paper proposes Self-Retrospection Distillation (SRD), a method that uses information from completed trajectories to train the same policy to make predictions before acting. Evaluated on 10 tool-integrated reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks, SRD complements RLVR and self-distillation baselines, with its benefit most pronounced when reward contrast is scarce. entry.summary: TULIP: Targeted LLM Unlearning at Layers Identified Per-input arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper examines representation-level unlearning in LLMs, where existing methods apply a single fixed layer to the entire forget set, and asks whether that is sufficient. The authors propose TULIP, which for each input uses the logit lens to locate the layer where the forget answer is formed and read out, then removes the hidden state's alignment with that answer's unembedding vector at that layer. The paper reports that TULIP outperforms output- and representation-level baselines on TOFU, PISTOL, and WMDP across Llama, Qwen, and Zephyr models, and remains robust to paraphrase and quantization attacks. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes TULIP, per-input layer selection for unlearning; the authors' hijacking experiment shows answers form at intermediate layers, and they report gains over baselines on TOFU, PISTOL, and WMDP, p

entry.title: One Leak, Lasting Gains: Binding Keys to Context to Deter Collusion
entry.summary: When One Leak Pays Forever: Context Binding and the Price of Deterring Collusion arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies collusion in threshold-encrypted mempools, where a coalition of decryption committee members that sells its decryption capability to a front-runner can expose every later block the capability still decrypts. The authors show that deterrence holds if and only if each coalition's penalty covers the largest discounted value a single leak can reach. Binding each leak to its own round, such as with per-epoch keys, lowers the required stake substantially. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model collusive key leaks in threshold-encrypted mempools as a repeated game, prove penalties must cover the largest discounted single-leak value, and give horizon-dependent tight bounds.

entry.title: SlideDP: Scaling Host-Resident LLM Fine-Tuning Across Multiple GPUs
entry.summary: SlideDP: Scaling Host-Resident LLM Fine-Tuning Across Multiple GPUs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper presents SlideDP, a synchronous data-parallel runtime for fine-tuning large language models that exceed GPU memory, using host-resident state on multi-GPU systems. entry.title: CAST: Faster language model decoding by checking more draft candidates at once
entry.summary: CAST: Cost-Aware Speculative Trees from One-Pass Block Drafters arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Speculative decoding speeds up large language models by cheaply drafting future tokens and verifying them in parallel. CAST packs the candidates a one-pass block drafter already scored into a tree and verifies it in a single target-model pass, without changing the model, drafter weights, or decoding rule. Tree width adapts automatically using a latency measurement rather than a width sweep. The authors report speedups over the standard chain in all eight tested settings, up to 43%, and prove the target output distribution is unchanged. ★★★★ Notable: CAST packs already-scored block-drafter candidates into a verification tree with cost-adaptive width. entry.title: ESTHER: Estimating and Reconstructing 3D Hands from Wearable Stereo Cameras in the Wild
entry.summary: ESTHER: Egocentric Stereo Hand Estimation and Reconstruction in the Wild arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper presents ESTHER, a model that estimates and reconstructs metric 3D hand structure from egocentric stereo cameras worn by a person. The authors also build ESTHER3D, a dataset with model-generated labels for in-the-wild training and motion-capture ground truth for testing. entry.title: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Reveal If Two VAE Codebooks Agree
entry.summary: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Show Whether Two Codebooks on a VAE's Latent Space Agree arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Many systems read a variational autoencoder's latent space as discrete codes and assume each latent is decoded as the code it was written as. The paper proves that no item in a standard training report can show whether written and read codes agree on encoded data. It builds two VAEs with perfect reconstruction, exact inference, and identical ELBO and code histograms, yet with agreement of 1 and 0. The ELBO's terms bound how far agreement can shift, and the authors test this on probabilistic PCA and 240 trained VAEs, proposing a protocol called Certify-or-Measure. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove standard training reports cannot reveal code agreement, build two VAEs with identical metrics but different agreement, derive ELBO-based shift bounds, and report checks on pPCA and 2

entry.title: What Language Models Can Inherit from Solomonoff Induction: Limits and Attainable Properties
entry.summary: What Can Language Models Inherit from Solomonoff Induction? Limits, Attainable Properties, and What Served Conditionals Reveal arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper tests the claim that scaling language models brings them closer to Solomonoff induction, using known results from algorithmic information theory, universal prediction, and Bayesian consistency. It argues that in its uniform form the claim fails for every computable model, so any closeness can only hold pointwise, one environment at a time. The authors also discuss which Solomonoff-like properties, such as in-context learning as amortised Bayesian inference, can be inherited and which a deployed system should have or avoid. ★★★★ Notable: Using Kraft inequality and known algorithmic information theory results, the authors argue language models cannot uniformly inherit Solomonoff guarantees, so closeness holds only pointwise.

entry.title: Auditing vision-language model benchmarks using saved evaluation outputs
entry.summary: Auditing VLM Benchmarks from Existing Evaluation Runs arXiv · Oct 9, 2026The paper adds an audit layer to VLMEvalKit that reuses per-question outputs saved from existing evaluation runs, applying six detectors plus one text-only rerun with images removed. Auditing MMStar, a benchmark built so images are essential, with three models, the authors find zero aggregate accuracy gain from the image on 20.2% of questions. After a permutation-null correction, the excess is concentrated in mathematics and science categories. ★★★★ Notable: Reuses existing VLM evaluation artifacts to audit benchmarks; item-matched permutation nulls show a +3.2 pp image-gain excess on MMStar, concentrated in math and science.

entry.title: How AI Models Differ in Accepting False Facts Planted Earlier in a Chat
entry.summary: Epistemic Policy Divergence in Multi-Turn LLM Contamination: A Protocol-Gradient Investigation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper studies session-level contamination, where false premises inserted in earlier conversation turns are later adopted as fact by large language models. The authors define five protocols ordered by source authority and test three models over 22,500 turns, finding that the models follow structurally different policies, with adoption rising sharply under system-injected authority and instruction override. The evaluation framework and taxonomy are released for reproducible testing. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes authority-gradient multi-turn contamination protocols; the authors report three models with distinct epistemic policies, with Gemini adoption ranging from 0.1% to 94.0% by framing.

entry.summary: Have I Seen Enough? The paper finds that unmodified frozen models already encode this readiness signal in a linearly readable form, labelled from timestamped evidence rather than model output. entry.summary: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper introduces Opera, a verbal critic framework that helps long-horizon coding agents receive corrective feedback. Each correction is kept as a persistent note and tracked until the diagnosed problem is resolved, with feedback audited against visible evidence before delivery. The authors report that Opera raises the resolve rate of non-critic agents on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a SWE-Bench Pro subset, and DeepSWE v1.1. entry.summary: CoDR: Training-Free Confidence-Drift Remasking for Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Masked diffusion language models decode by committing tokens to masked positions, and these commitments are usually irreversible, so early mistakes can propagate. entry.summary: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks arXiv · Oct 6, 2026LLM agents often lack operational knowledge of new environments and repeat the same mistakes without memory of past attempts. entry.summary: HERO: Histology Encoder for Robust Representation in Oncology arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This report introduces HERO, a ViT-G/14 pathology foundation model trained with DINO and iBOT objectives on 500 million tiles from about 575,000 clinical whole-slide images. entry.title: Simple deterministic auctions for selling multiple items
entry.summary: On the Power of Determinism in Multi-Item Auctions arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies a single buyer with multiple items whose values are independent but not necessarily identically distributed. entry.title: PHASE: A physiology-guided foundation model for intracranial EEG
entry.summary: PHASE: A Physiology-Guided Hierarchical Foundation Model for Intracranial EEG arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces PHASE, a foundation model for intracranial EEG that makes directly measurable physiological characteristics explicit learning targets. entry.title: Representation risk: pretrained image encoders can change predictive conclusions
entry.summary: Representation Risk in Pretrained Image Encoders arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper argues that the pretrained image encoder used to turn pictures into features is a source of model uncertainty, which the authors call representation risk. Ten frozen encoders were compared across tasks including house prices, racehorse performance, histology, chest radiographs, facial age, and rice disease, with the encoder chosen on locked validation data. The results show no single encoder is best everywhere, and the authors recommend benchmarking candidates, selecting on validation data, and reporting paired and split-level uncertainty. The workflow is implemented in the LOOKAGAIN-ML software package. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes representation risk, showing that ten frozen image encoders across six applications yield large validation-selected test gaps, e.g., house-price R² rising from 0.396 to 0.629.

entry.summary: Closing a single-copy gap to the Holevo bound with two-copy measurements arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies whether the Holevo Cramér-Rao bound for quantum multiparameter estimation can be attained with finite copies of a state. For orthogonal leakage, the miss probability is asymptotically 4/M, independent of the ambient dimension. Measuring all references first yields zero detection under the same zero-false-alarm requirement. entry.title: Evanescent-wave Johnson noise from superconductors, explained
entry.summary: Evanescent-wave Johnson Noise from Superconductors arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper calculates evanescent-wave Johnson noise above a superconductor's surface and the resulting relaxation time T1 of spin and charge qubits placed nanometers away. It uses a microscopic current-response kernel for a BCS superconductor, together with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and nonlocal surface impedances. entry.title: Near-optimal quantum simulation of open-system lattice dynamics, explained
entry.summary: Near-optimal quantum simulation of lattice Lindbladian dynamics arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how to simulate time evolution under geometrically local Lindbladians on a lattice of qudits. The authors present an algorithm that approximates this evolution for time t on N qudits, with diamond-norm error ε, using geometrically local circuits of depth O(t polylog(Nt/ε)). The authors state that this performance is comparable to the HHKL algorithm for lattice Hamiltonian simulation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend HHKL lattice Hamiltonian simulation to geometrically local Lindbladians, reporting local circuits of depth O(t polylog(Nt/ε)) comparable to HHKL.

entry.title: Near-optimal parallel quantum gate learning with low diamond-distance error
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Parallel Unitary Process Tomography in Diamond Distance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how to learn an unknown quantum gate (unitary process tomography), a key step toward working quantum computers. Sequential circuits were already known to achieve optimal query complexity under diamond-distance error, but it was unclear whether parallel circuits could match this. The authors introduce a new explicit parallel procedure and prove that near-optimal query complexity is achievable with parallel circuits. The gap between parallel and sequential approaches is thus closed up to a logarithmic factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an explicit parallel procedure that reaches near-optimal query complexity in diamond distance, narrowing the gap to sequential circuits to a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Is rapid mixing stable? A study of whether fast relaxation in open quantum systems survives local perturbations
entry.summary: Is rapid mixing stable? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Many open quantum systems governed by Lindbladians relax to steady states quickly, in polylogarithmic time in system size. The paper questions whether local perturbations leave this fast mixing intact. It gives counterexamples showing rapid mixing is not stable in general, even when the steady state is unchanged, and shows arbitrarily weak local Hamiltonian perturbations can destroy it. It also provides sufficient conditions guaranteeing stable rapid mixing for several classes of systems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show rapid mixing is generally unstable via counterexamples and give several sufficient conditions for stable rapid mixing, including quasifree fermionic, commuting, and local spin systems

entry.title: Fast Hamiltonian engineering via cut polytope geometry
entry.summary: Fast Hamiltonian engineering from cut polytope geometry arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for Hamiltonian engineering, which simulates a target Hamiltonian's quantum dynamics using a native entangling system and restricted controls, across 2-local qubit, qudit, and fermionic systems. The authors recast time-optimal engineering as a k-cut polytope problem, prove it NP-complete, and relax it to an elliptope with Krivine-type rounding to generate pulses for a linear program. On Ising, chiral clock, and fermionic Harper-Hofstadter benchmarks, the method achieves near-optimal run times and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, with an O(√m) approximation ratio. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce time-optimal Hamiltonian engineering to a complex k-cut polytope problem, report NP-completeness, and obtain an O(√m) approximation via elliptope relaxation with Krivine rounding, r

entry.title: Digital quantum algorithms for creating and using spin squeezed states
entry.summary: Digital Quantum Algorithms for Generating and Utilizing Spin Squeezed States arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents algorithms for efficiently generating and using spin squeezed states on digital quantum computers. The authors introduce an adaptive local-circuit protocol that prepares states with squeezing parameter ξ in depth O(log 1/ξ), which they prove is optimal for permutation symmetric states. entry.title: Chern-number estimation: near-optimal quantum algorithm with provable speedup
entry.summary: Chern-number estimation: nearly optimal quantum algorithm and provable quantum speedup arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm for estimating the Chern number, a topological invariant, of a smooth Hamiltonian family over a two-dimensional parameter torus with a unique gapped ground state, including interacting many-body systems. Its Hamiltonian-oracle evolution time is Õ(L_xL_y/Δ_min³), and the authors prove a matching worst-case oracle lower bound, even when the Chern number is promised to be zero or one, so the algorithm is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. entry.title: Proving that deciding whether the multiparameter quantum Fisher information is attainable is NP-hard
entry.summary: Deciding the Attainability of the Multiparameter Quantum Fisher Information is NP-Hard arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The quantum Fisher information sets a bound on the precision of estimating several parameters at once, but a general condition for reaching this bound with measurements on single copies of a state has been missing. This paper proves that deciding exact attainability is NP-hard, even for a restricted class of real, constant-rank quantum models. The proof reduces from deciding whether a bipartite density matrix is separable. Unless P=NP, no efficiently computable necessary and sufficient criterion exists in general. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report reducing multiparameter QFI attainability to separability and proving it NP-hard, presented as a resolution of a long-open question and a fundamental computational obstruction.

entry.summary: One-dimensional quantum Gibbs states in constant circuit depth arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proves that the Gibbs state of any spin chain at any constant temperature is exactly a mixture of product states over bounded-length blocks of qubits. This implies such states can be prepared by constant-depth local unitary circuits with efficient classical preprocessing. entry.title: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm: Tight Query Bounds for Solving Linear Equations on Quantum Computers
entry.summary: An Optimal Quantum Linear Systems Algorithm arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies the quantum linear systems problem, where one has query access to a sparse matrix A with condition number κ and must produce a quantum state approximating the solution x of Ax = b. The authors show the query complexity is Θ(κ√d·log(1/ε)), improving previous upper and lower bounds. They also resolve an open question of Berry and Childs by showing any N×N unitary can be implemented with bounded error using O(√N) matrix-entry queries. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a tight Θ(κ√d log(1/ε)) query bound for quantum linear systems, improving prior bounds and resolving an open problem of Berry and Childs.

entry.title: The Power of Oracle Access: Optimal Complexity for the Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem
entry.summary: The power of oracle access: Optimal sample and query complexity of the abelian state hidden subgroup problem arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the state hidden subgroup problem, which asks for the symmetries of an unknown quantum state. For finite abelian groups, it gives a query-model algorithm using O(log(|G/H|)/√ε) forward and inverse queries together with a matching lower bound. In the sample model it shows Θ(log(|G/H|)/ε) copies are necessary and sufficient. The quadratic improvement in ε therefore comes from coherent access to the preparation circuit. ★★★★★ Notable: The paper studies the abelian state hidden subgroup problem, giving an O(log|G/H|/√ε) query algorithm with a matching lower bound and Θ(log|G/H|/ε) sample complexity, with applications to stabilizer g

entry.title: Exponential lower bounds for low-degree strategies in quantum position-based cryptography
entry.summary: Exponential lower bounds for low-degree strategies in position-based quantum cryptography arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies lower bounds on the resources needed for non-local quantum computation (NLQC), in which two distant players cooperatively implement a bipartite unitary. The authors consider a family of diagonal ±1 unitaries indexed by Boolean hypercube elements and show that, under a low-degree polynomial condition on the first round, implementing at least one of them requires resources growing exponentially. The result matters for the security of position-based quantum cryptography, and the proof relies on type constants of particular Banach spaces and random estimates of Boolean functions. ★★★★ Notable: Addressing the open problem of exponential NLQC lower bounds, the authors report resource scaling of exp(Ω(n^{2δ}/(log n)^2)) for low-degree strategies, proved via Banach space type constants.

entry.title: How fast can a parent estimate its children's value? A quantum algorithm for stochastic games
entry.summary: How fast can a parent estimate the value of their children? A quantum algorithm for stochastic games arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm for two-player stochastic games whose trees alternate adversarial and chance layers. It estimates the game's value using queries to leaf values and gives an upper bound on the query complexity. The authors show that quadratic speedups known for adversarial trees and single expectations both carry over when nested. ★★★★ Notable: Gives a depth-exponential bound nesting quantum adversarial search with mean estimation; the authors report both quadratic speedups survive the composition.

entry.title: Generalized LIMDDs: Compact, Canonical Decision Diagrams Modulo a Group
entry.summary: Generalized LIMDDs: Succinctness and Canonicity for Decision Diagrams Modulo a Group arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper studies decision diagrams for functions from {0,1}^n to C, where residual nodes are merged when they lie in one orbit of a group and the group element is recorded on edges. The group family is generated by phase rotations of order q with up to k control qubits, with or without bit flip X. The authors show exponential succinctness gains over Pauli-LIMDD, and give a five-rule reduction system with unique normal forms computable in polynomial time. ★★★★ Notable: Generalizes Myhill-Nerode quotients to group actions, reporting exponential succinctness gains over Pauli-LIMDD and a unique normal form computable in polynomial time.

entry.title: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for learning open quantum system dynamics
entry.summary: Gauge freedom and efficient algorithms for Lindbladian learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies learning a local Lindbladian, which describes open quantum system dynamics, in the presence of state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) noise. SPAM noise can make distinct Lindbladians experimentally indistinguishable, so part of the Lindbladian is unlearnable. The authors characterize this obstruction and present SPAM-robust algorithms that learn every universally gauge-invariant component using only trusted single-qubit operations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show SPAM noise can make distinct Lindbladians indistinguishable, characterize gauge freedom, and give SPAM-robust learning algorithms using Õ(ε⁻²log(N/δ)) experiments and evolution time.

entry.summary: Weakly interacting fermionic Gibbs states are Gaussian mixtures and classically simulable arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper proves that for sufficiently weak interactions, the Gibbs state of a local fermionic Hamiltonian at any finite temperature and in any spatial dimension is a convex mixture of fermionic Gaussian states. entry.summary: Log-Euclidean Rényi Conditional Mutual Information arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper introduces a quantum Rényi conditional mutual information that measures conditional independence between quantum systems. entry.summary: Simultaneously Query-Optimal Quantum Linear-System Algorithm arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper asks whether one quantum algorithm for linear systems can meet the known optimal query bounds for both the matrix block-encoding oracle and the right-hand-side state-preparation oracle at once. entry.title: Controlling risk in LLM answers by pricing label-free checks
entry.summary: Risk-Controlled Selective LLM Answering by Pricing Label-Free Checks arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper introduces PriceCheck, which builds decision rules from label-free checks such as re-solving a problem to decide when a large language model should answer or abstain. Each check is priced by its agreement rates on correct and incorrect answers and its cost per run. In mathematics, the selected schedules served 76.1% of answers on average while keeping held-out selective risk below 1.5% on all 15 splits. ★★★★ Notable: PriceCheck combines priced label-free checks into abstention rules; on math it reports 76.1% average coverage with held-out selective risk below 1.5% on 15 splits, beating reward models and judges.

entry.title: Revisiting dual lattice attacks on bounded distance decoding with a heuristic-free trade-off
entry.summary: Dual lattice attacks for bounded distance decoding, revisited arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper examines the assumption that scores of short dual vectors in dual lattice attacks are mutually independent. In the Haar-random lattice model, without heuristic assumptions, the authors prove an explicit asymptotic trade-off between target radius and query time for decision bounded distance decoding with preprocessing. Using Siegel and Rogers moment identities, they analyze cosine scores over complete dual balls and bound error probabilities. The resulting trade-off matches the asymptotic prediction of the Ducas-Pulles conditional model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an explicit asymptotic BDD preprocessing trade-off in the Haar-random lattice model without heuristics, which they state matches the Ducas-Pulles conditional prediction.

entry.title: Relevance Is Not Sufficient Evidence: Spotting Missing Facts in RAG Before Answering
entry.summary: Relevance Is Not Sufficient Evidence: Detecting Evidence Gaps Before Generation in RAG arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper examines retrieval-augmented generation, where retrieved passages may name the right entities but lack the facts needed to answer. It reports that 12 generators still answered 40.0-99.3% of insufficient-evidence questions even when told to abstain. The authors build a paired benchmark and propose RINSE, which combines question coverage, answer presence in passages, and a small language model's judgment to assess sufficiency before generation. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes RINSE, judging evidence sufficiency before generation from question and passages; reports 0.837 average across six datasets, above best baseline 0.746 and a frontier model at 0.784.

entry.title: Evidence that LLM internal activations encode explore and exploit modes in semantic search
entry.summary: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines whether large language models, when listing concepts in a semantic fluency task, internally represent the same explore and exploit search modes found in humans. Using interpretability methods such as the Jacobian lens, the authors show that activations predict when the model switches between categories. They also show that steering these activations changes how often switching occurs. ★★★★ Notable: Extends semantic foraging to LLM internals; the authors report that J-lens activations track category switching and that steering vectors causally bias switching rates.

entry.title: Do VGGT-Family Models Need All Their Layers? A Study of Layer Redundancy and Pruning
entry.summary: Does the VGGT Family Need All Its Layers? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This study examines which layers of the feed-forward geometry models VGGT, π³, and VGGT-Ω are needed to preserve camera poses and dense 3D structure. It evaluates 3,018 pruned configurations on seven metrics across four indoor and outdoor datasets, finding removable layers concentrated in an early region and a narrower late region. A closed-form linear calibration recovers accuracy after pruning without end-to-end retraining. The resulting models reduce aggregator parameters by up to 44% while keeping accuracy comparable to the intact models. ★★★★ Notable: Studies layer redundancy across 3,018 pruned VGGT-family configurations, reporting two redundancy regions and closed-form calibration that recovers accuracy with up to 44% fewer aggregator parameters.

entry.title: On-policy distillation that reflects on visual evidence to train visual agents
entry.summary: On-Policy Visual Evidence Distillation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Visual agents alternate between reasoning and image operations, so early errors in acquiring, reading, or grounding visual evidence can propagate through the trajectory. The paper introduces ReVuE, which compares multiple student trajectories for the same query, summarizes observed visual evidence, and diagnoses the first failure across the Acquire, Read, and Ground stages. These reflections give the teacher training-time context, and token-level distillation losses are grouped and reweighted accordingly. entry.summary: You Cannot Recover What Was Never Measured: Quantifying the Information Ceiling of Ultra-Low-Field MRI Super-Resolution arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The study measures how much subject-specific information real 64 mT portable MRI scans actually contain, using paired scans of the same subjects at 3T. entry.title: RESCUE: Fixing Language Model Errors by Repairing Sparse Circuits with Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: RESCUE: Repairing Language Model Errors to Sparse Circuits via Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces RESCUE, a framework that locates sparse internal circuits linked to language model errors and fine-tunes only those parameters to repair the failures. It uses reinforcement learning with multiple masked-model rollouts to refine the circuit masks so they better match failures that occur during generation. On math reasoning and medical QA repair sets, the identified circuits have densities of 1.40% and 1.44%, and repair-set accuracy rises from 6.0% to 75.5% and from 0% to 81%. ★★★★ Notable: Extends circuit analysis to error repair with RL-refined masks; reports large repair-set accuracy gains on math and medical QA.

entry.title: Spotter: Embodied Model Leads, Vision-Language Model Reflects and Corrects Errors
entry.summary: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper finds that current embodied robot models rarely repair their own failures on retry. The authors propose Spotter, in which the embodied model executes continuously while a vision-language model (VLM) monitors in parallel and intervenes only when an error is confirmed, reflecting on and correcting it before returning control. Experiments on RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0 and a real robot show improved success rates, with successful episodes taking only modestly longer than the embodied model alone. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes reversing VLM-led control: the embodied model leads, and the VLM monitors in parallel, intervening only on detected errors, with reported gains on RoboCasa, RoboTwin, and a real robot.

entry.title: MyoCodec: A Streaming Neural Codec for Muscle Electrical Signals
entry.summary: MyoCodec: A Streaming Neural Codec for Electromyography arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents MyoCodec, a streaming neural codec for electromyography (EMG), the recording of muscle electrical activity. It combines causal Transformers with residual vector quantization to encode EMG signals into representations from continuous features to discrete tokens at 50 Hz. entry.summary: Do LLMs Really Forget? entry.summary: Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper finds that pretrained transformers use little depth to follow in-context references, reliably tracing only about 1.4 to 3.6 lines across thirteen base models. entry.title: CounterSteer: Blocking Hidden Instructions in AI Agent Tool Results

entry.summary: Large-scale factor analysis shows machine intelligence is only partially interpretable arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper applies factor analysis, a psychometric method, to 13,251 evaluation scores from 1,618 language models across 456 text-only benchmarks to test whether a general intelligence factor exists. entry.title: LLMs Learn to Evade Latent Monitors from Prior Feedback Alone: language models learning to hide internal activity from detectors using feedback.
entry.summary: LLMs Learn to Evade Latent Monitors from Prior Feedback Alone arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies whether latent-space monitors, which inspect LLM internal activations to detect undesired behavior, can be evaded by agents. Models inferred the monitor's decision rule from prior verdicts and edited activations accordingly. Scaling edits by 8x cut the monitor's true positive rate from 100% to 27%, and a rank-1 LoRA reduced it to 4% on held-out concept monitors while retaining benchmark capabilities. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show models can infer latent monitor rules from feedback alone and edit activations to evade detection, reporting TPR falling to 27% with scaling and 4% with rank-1 LoRA.

entry.title: Degree balance sets a fine-grained complexity boundary for quantum SAT
entry.summary: Degree Balance as a Fine-Grained Complexity Boundary for Quantum SAT arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the local Hamiltonian problem, a QMA-complete problem, under fine-grained complexity. Assuming the Hamiltonian is frustration-free on YES instances and approximately regular, the authors give classical and quantum algorithms that are exponentially faster than brute force. Assuming (Q)SETH, they show quantum 5-SAT has no non-trivial worst-case speedup, even when only O(√n) qubits have high degree. Reducing that high-degree set or its degrees by a factor of n^δ yields an O(2^{(1-ε)n}) algorithm. ★★★★ Notable: Under frustration-freeness and approximate regularity, the authors give exponential speedups and report a (Q)SETH lower bound nearly matching this boundary, forming a fine-grained dichotomy.

entry.summary: RA-CFGCache: From Branch-Level Criteria to Guided-Risk Control under Classifier-Free Guidance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper addresses the high computational cost of diffusion models under classifier-free guidance, which requires both conditional and unconditional evaluations. It proposes RA-CFGCache, a training-free caching framework that accounts for how cache errors combine across branches and how local errors affect the final output at different timesteps. entry.title: Longer Records, Broader Invariance: Scaling Pitfalls in Longitudinal Contrastive Learning
entry.summary: Longer Records, Broader Invariance: The Hidden Scaling Problem in Longitudinal Contrastive Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how contrastive learning on longitudinal data, which treats observations from the same person as positives, can erase meaningful behavioral change as records grow longer. The authors separate record span from supervision span and find, using in-home sensing records up to 2.7 years, that broader supervision suppresses recoverable changing-state information. They also report a prospective replication in 199 GLOBEM participants. ★★★★ Notable: Separates record span from supervision span; the authors report longer histories broaden invariance, reversible via same-person contrast, and reproduce the effect prospectively in 199 participants.

entry.title: Neural Succession: An Ecology-Inspired Theory of Forgetting in Continual Learning
entry.summary: Neural Succession: A Mesoscopic Theory of Invasion, Coexistence, and Stabilization in Continual Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes Successional Learning Theory (SLT), which frames continual learning as an ecological process in which a current representation is a resident community and a new task is an invader that can displace it. Its key measure, directional pre-invasion compatibility, is computed on the resident model before the new task is learned and is strongly negatively correlated with later forgetting (r=-0.789 across 20 Split-CIFAR-10 transitions). The authors position SLT as a pre-adaptation diagnostic that complements replay, regularization, and projection methods. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a mesoscopic succession-based theory of continual learning in which pre-invasion compatibility predicts forgetting, with the authors reporting results across eight experiments.

entry.title: Audience-bound persistent memory: authorization across the whole memory lifecycle
entry.summary: Audience-Bound Persistent Memory: Authorization Across the Memory Lifecycle arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how a personal language agent acting for its owner across private and shared conversations should authorize memory before assembling context. Each memory item records the audience present when it was made, and a memory enters a model's context only if every current viewer belongs to an authorized audience. The approach was implemented in two independent architectures and an agent-memory runtime. In a pre-registered test over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered any architecture's context, while unscoped retrieval exposed forbidden items in 82% of contexts. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes audience-bound memory admission across the lifecycle; over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered context while unscoped retrieval exposed them in 82%.

entry.title: Algorithm for Arctic product-mix auction equilibria
entry.summary: Solving the Arctic Product-Mix Auction arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies Arctic product-mix auctions, where budget-constrained bidders express preferences over multiple substitute goods. It gives the first strongly polynomial algorithm for finding competitive equilibria when the auctioneer has separable convex piecewise-linear costs. entry.title: Training LLMs to Say When They Know They're Being Evaluated
entry.summary: Training LLMs to Verbalize Evaluation Awareness arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Language models may act differently during audits when they are aware they are being evaluated, which makes such behavior hard to measure. entry.summary: CyFA: Linear Sequence Modeling with Relative-Time-Partitioned Memory arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper introduces CyFA (Cyclic Flow Attention), a linear RNN whose memory is partitioned by relative time. entry.title: Influence maximization in near-linear time: a faster method for choosing key seed nodes
entry.summary: Maximizing Social Influence in Almost Linear Time arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies influence maximization, which seeks k seed nodes in a graph with n nodes and m edges to maximize expected information spread under standard diffusion models. entry.summary: From Classical to Quantum Channels: Achieving Positive Covert Rates arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines when covert communication at positive rates is possible over discrete memoryless classical, classical-quantum, and quantum channels. For classical point-to-point channels, positive covert rates are achievable for certain channel classes when the input alphabet is larger than the output alphabet. For quantum channels, if the innocent state is mixed, a non-trivial input ensemble can always satisfy the covertness constraint. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give new conditions for positive covert rates over classical, cq, and quantum channels, extending to MACs; they report that input dimension exceeding output dimension yields achievability.

entry.summary: Reasoning with Neural Cellular Automata arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper tests whether Neural Cellular Automata, networks using only local connectivity and asynchronous updates, can perform complex multi-step reasoning. entry.title: Rendering Inputs as Images to Defend Against Prompt Injection
entry.summary: Render Before Reading: Visual Rendering as a Prompt Injection Defense arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper finds that multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instructions delivered as text than when the same instructions arrive as images.
