entry.summary: Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper introduces Mnemon, a memory agent for LLM assistants that keeps conversations as raw dated records instead of rewriting them at write time. An LLM plans searches, a fast decision model called Jev judges the returned records, and explicit budget rules assemble a small context for the answering model. The authors report top scores on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with small per-question context and slow cost growth on the BEAM benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: Splits memory work into fast batch judgments over raw dated records and slow LLM planning; the authors report 91.7% on LoCoMo and 83.8% on LongMemEval-S.

entry.title: Proof that the best known bound for preferent compression is tight
entry.summary: Preferent Compression Bounds Are Tight arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper concerns sample compression, a method for producing safety and performance guarantees for learning-based systems. Sharp bounds exist for algorithms with a preference (stability) property, but whether they are tight was an open question. The authors show the current best bound is tight, using an explicit construction based on the uniform distribution and order statistics. They also give a shorter proof relying only on elementary counting. ★★★★ Notable: Addresses whether preferent compression bounds are tight, reporting an explicit uniform-distribution construction that attains the bound in the limit, plus a shorter elementary proof.

entry.title: Same Text, Different Authority: How Reserved Tokens Make Chat-Template Prompt Injection Stronger
entry.summary: Same Bytes, Different Authority: Reserved-Token Representations in Chat-Template Prompt Injection arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies prompt injection against LLM agents, finding that forged chat-template markers such as <|im_start|> are far more effective when fed to the model as reserved control tokens than as ordinary subwords. Encoding the same text as subwords lowered attack success on the InjecAgent benchmark by 39 to 66 percentage points on three of four open-weight families. The standard tokenizer mitigation covers only tokens a configuration declares special, so tool-protocol tokens remain unprotected and the gap persists on that channel. ★★★★★ Notable: Shows that the same text encoded as a reserved control token versus subwords changes forged-marker injection authority, quantified on InjecAgent and AgentDojo, with implications for defense.

entry.title: MMSkillRisk: Can AI agents stay safe when image-based skills hide malicious instructions?
entry.summary: MMSkillRisk: Can Agents Stay Safe When Multimodal Skills Become Traps? arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper introduces MMSkillRisk, a benchmark for end-to-end safety testing of attacks hidden in images within multimodal agent skills. The authors design NCVA, an attack that disguises malicious instructions as native parts of teaching images, such as annotations and interface labels. Across nine model-harness configurations, NCVA reaches a pooled attack success rate of 43.1%, 16.4 percentage points above a text-carrier baseline. The results show attacks can succeed while legitimate tasks are also completed, so task success alone does not prove safe skill use. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report that NCVA, an image-borne attack, reaches 43.1% pooled ASR in isolated sandboxes, 16.4 points above the text-carrier baseline across nine configurations.

entry.summary: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Token consumption by a large language model agent can vary widely across runs of the same task, and growing context raises the input cost of each later call. entry.summary: λ-JEPA Spectral Anti-Collapse Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies representation collapse in joint-embedding self-supervised learning, finding that anti-collapse objectives applied after a projection head may not prevent dimensional collapse in the backbone. entry.summary: Learning sparse quantum states from single-qubit measurements arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies learning sparse quantum states, whose density matrices have at most s nonzero entries in an unknown product basis. A key component is a quantum-succinct claw-state generation protocol that uses classical communication to expand a few quantum correlations into many claw-state correlations. entry.summary: Can LLMs Value the Right Evidence? entry.summary: ReSS: Residual-Restoring Sparse Attention for 3D Vision Transformers arXiv · Sep 29, 20263D vision transformers such as VGGT estimate camera poses and scene geometry from multiple images in one pass, but their attention cost grows quickly with the number of views. This paper proposes ReSS, which selects blocks to drop by minimizing the drift that sparsification leaves in the residual stream, rather than by keeping high attention probability. entry.title: AI Virus Spreading via Shared Files Between LLM Agents
entry.summary: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how large language model assistants that share persistent artifacts, such as reports, can unintentionally pass adversarial content between one another. Malicious content is stored in an assistant's memory, reproduced in later artifacts, and picked up by other assistants. The authors simulate artifact exchange among independent assistants to measure survival across hand-offs, hop count, and spread. They report that attacks propagate across multiple assistants and reach 60-80% of agents in larger simulations, with chains extending to eight hops. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a self-propagating attack spreading via shared artifacts across independent assistants, reporting 60-80% agent reach and eight-hop chains in larger simulations.

entry.summary: Universal Approximation of Measure-to-Measure Operators by Pushforwards arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies whether continuous operators between spaces of probability measures can be approximated by pushforward models whose transformation depends on the input distribution. entry.summary: Manifold-Stable Flow Matching arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper introduces manifold-stable flow matching (MSFM), which can start from an arbitrary ambient prior, not necessarily supported on the data manifold. It uses contraction theory to combine learned tangential transport with prescribed normal contraction, using analytical projectors for known manifolds and PCA-estimated local affine proxies for unknown ones. entry.title: SOLO: Training Billion-Parameter Language Models Locally with a Shared Output Readout
entry.summary: SOLO: Pretraining Billion-Parameter Language Models with Shared-Output Local Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes SOLO (Shared-Output LOcal learning), which replaces each module's private readout with a shared, read-only copy of the final module's readout, so that every module receives information from the whole network without passing gradients between modules. On Transformers with 340M to 2B parameters pretrained on 15B tokens, SOLO stays within one point of backpropagation in average zero-shot accuracy. Because it avoids update locking, it allows larger micro-batches, reaching up to 1.44x the best throughput of pipeline backpropagation on the same partition. ★★★★★ Notable: Replaces private module readouts with a shared read-only output copy; the abstract reports near-backprop results at 340M–2B scale and up to 1.44x pipeline throughput.

entry.summary: Convex Optimization Is Free When Accuracy Is Expensive arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies convex optimization when gradients can only be approximated, with computational cost growing as δ^(-γ) in accuracy δ. It introduces a randomized multilevel oracle that gives an unbiased estimator of the approximation, lowering the cost of one call to δ^(2-γ)σ^(-2). entry.title: Lasting Partners Push Up Prices Among Learning Pricing Agents
entry.summary: Persistent Partners Raise Prices Among Learning Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies pricing agents that repeatedly meet on a platform, asking whether the platform's choice of who faces whom changes the prices the agents learn. Using the Bertrand duopoly model of Calvano et al., prices are set by tabular Q-learning, with randomized assignment of keeping the same partner, seeing rival prices, and messaging. Keeping the same partner raised average training-period profit levels by 0.27 of the gap between competitive and monopoly profit (95% CI 0.20 to 0.35). ★★★★ Notable: A preregistered experiment reports fixed partners lift learned-agent profit levels by 0.27 and separates learned punishment from static best response, for algorithmic collusion research.

entry.title: First learn, then memorize: why diffusion models generalize before they memorize
entry.summary: First Learn, Then Memorize: The Spectral Bias of Diffusion Models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies why diffusion models trained on a finite dataset first generate novel samples and only later collapse onto their training set. The authors show that training dynamics are governed by the Neural Tangent Kernel Gram matrix on noisy data, and that repeated noising splits its spectrum into a large-eigenvalue part linked to generalization and a small-eigenvalue part linked to memorization. Analytical results in high-dimensional limits and experiments on CelebA and U-Nets support this picture, and truncating the Gram matrix or penalizing the second bulk is shown to tune the transition. ★★★★ Notable: The authors explain diffusion models' generalize-then-memorize timescales via two spectral bulks of the NTK Gram matrix, reporting analysis plus CelebA and U-Net experiments and causal interventions.

entry.title: How weighting schedules control what score-based generative models learn from multimodal data, and when
entry.summary: Weighting Schedules Govern What and When Score-Based Generative Models Learn from Multimodal Data arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies how score-based generative models learn multimodal distributions during training. The authors split the time-integrated loss into single-time contributions and analyze each at a fixed signal-to-noise ratio, finding that this ratio sets how fast mode directions and relative weights are learned. At high signal-to-noise ratio, all mode directions are learned together on one timescale while relative weights are not learned. Near the speciation time, where the ratio is of order one, every feature becomes learnable on its own timescale. entry.title: Paper on how narrow multimodal fine-tuning can cause emergent misalignment in vision-language AI models
entry.summary: Narrow Multimodal Fine-Tuning Can Induce Emergent Misalignment arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies whether fine-tuning vision-language models on narrow multimodal tasks, such as vulnerable code, careless household-object use, and conspiratorial readings of ordinary scenes, can cause emergent misalignment. Across fifteen commercial and open-source models, the authors find that such fine-tuning induces broadly misaligned behavior that transfers to unrelated tasks. They also test mitigation strategies that partially reduce this effect. ★★★★★ Notable: First extension of narrow-task fine-tuning induced emergent misalignment to vision-language models; the authors report it transfers to unrelated tasks across fifteen commercial and open-source models

entry.title: AIM-ZO: Activation-guided subspace maintenance for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning without backpropagation
entry.summary: AIM-ZO: Activation-Informed Subspace Maintenance for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes AIM-ZO, a zeroth-order method for fine-tuning large language models that estimates updates using only forward evaluations, avoiding backpropagation and activation storage. It uses forward activations as local directional information and continuously integrates them into a broad, evolving subspace, while activating only a small set of shared and sampled directions per step. Across 5 LLMs and 11 downstream tasks under matched forward-evaluation budgets, its six-task average exceeds the strongest fully evaluated ZO baseline by 1.26 points on OPT-2.7B and MeZO by 2.85 points on OPT-30B. ★★★★ Notable: AIM-ZO uses forward activations as local direction cues within an evolving broad subspace; the authors report six-task averages 1.26 points above the best ZO baseline on OPT-2.7B and 2.85 points above

entry.title: Envy-free splits of random assignments, with four agents solved
entry.summary: Envy-Free Decompositions of Random Assignments: Settling Four Agents, and What Lies Beyond arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper studies whether a random assignment of objects to agents can be decomposed into deterministic assignments so that every agent envies any other with probability at most 1/2. It proves this is always possible for four agents using a computer-aided check over all vertices, and shows 1/2 is the best general threshold. It also gives proofs for special cases and shows some natural decomposition methods fail. Deciding whether an arbitrary random assignment admits such a decomposition is strongly NP-complete. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that every four-agent SD-EF random assignment admits a Dec-EF decomposition via a computer-aided proof, and prove strong NP-completeness for the general decision problem.

entry.title: Subgroup rank-1 lattice points for fast high-dimensional black-box integral estimation
entry.summary: Subgroup Rank-1 Lattice for Practical High-dimensional Black-box Integral Approximation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes subgroup rank-1 lattice point sets for estimating integrals of high-dimensional black-box functions, such as kernel mean embeddings and the softmax kernel in self-attention. Restricting the Korobov generator to a fixed multiplicative order allows feature-map computations to be done exactly by FFT in O(n log m) time and O(n) memory. The authors prove a convergence rate for the squared worst-case error and report better results than random features and scrambled Sobol' and Halton points across synthetic and real-data settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine subgroup rank-1 lattices with FFT to cut feature-map integration to O(n log m) time and O(n) memory, and report a worst-case error decay of O(n^{-(α-1)/(m-1)}) in the Korobov space

entry.title: AReaL-TIK: An agent that optimizes unified RL GPU kernels using a search-tracking representation
entry.summary: AReaL-TIK: Stateful Agentic Optimization of Unified RL Kernels through an Optimization IR arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Reinforcement learning post-training often uses separate GPU kernels for rollout and policy updates, and numerical differences can distort probability ratios. The paper introduces KernelBraid, an agentic framework that starts from a hand-tuned, bitwise-consistent unified kernel and organizes code search with an optimization intermediate representation. Changes are kept only if they pass correctness checks and improve aggregate latency. Across 12 end-to-end training setups on H20, it reaches 1.10x average throughput relative to AReaL with log-probability recomputation. ★★★★ Notable: KernelBraid uses an optimization IR to guide agentic search for bitwise-consistent RL kernels; the authors report 1.10x average throughput over AReaL across 12 end-to-end configurations.

entry.summary: Tool Mediation Alters Refusal Mechanisms in Large Language Models arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper examines why large language models are less likely to refuse harmful requests when they operate through external tools than in ordinary conversation. entry.title: Depot-closed multi-component construction for neural vehicle routing
entry.summary: Depot-Closed Multi-Component Construction for Neural Vehicle Routing arXiv · Sep 28, 2026Most neural solvers for vehicle routing build one route at a time until it is complete. This paper proposes multi-component construction, which keeps several route components at once and merges them in any order, treating each component as an implicitly depot-closed route so intermediate states are feasible. The merge cost reduction equals the Clarke-Wright saving. A policy trained only on CVRP100 reportedly outperforms representative neural solvers on CVRP100-500 and across capacities from 10 to 500 in a zero-shot evaluation. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes multi-component construction that keeps many route components at once, merging them in any order using Clarke-Wright savings; the authors report gains over listed neural solvers on CVRP100-50

entry.summary: Beyond Gradient Flow: Identifiability and Recovery from Distribution Snapshots arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper studies how to infer the dynamics of an evolving distribution from its snapshots. entry.summary: EMPIRIC: Experiment-Driven Learning of Residual World Models for Robot Planning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper presents EMPIRIC, an agent that extends a physics engine with learned code for mechanisms it lacks, such as glue curing, water heating, or wind.
